documentation_metadata.scope: Digital schematic of the Bally AS-2518-35 MPU board. Content is limited to facts derivable from the schematic and standard datasheets. No observer-specific or implementation-specific content (those belong in separate documents).
documentation_metadata.audience: Anyone designing or using a tool that interfaces with the AS-2518-35 (repair tools, monitors, emulators, educational references).
notes: Pin-level coverage of U7-U12 verified against schematic.
U9 CPU pin_detail includes all passive components on clock, IRQ, NMI, HALT, and VMA pins.
U12 chip identity confirmed as 555 timer in astable configuration.
All address decode logic (U17, U18, U19) and matrix topology fully captured.
Auxiliary lamp driver and main lamp driver are separate board profiles (see matrix_topology.lamp_matrix forward references).

board_info.description: Microprocessor Unit - Main game controller for Bally -35 pinball system
games: Multiple Bally pinball machines from the late 1970s through mid-1980s
version_notes: v1.6 addendum (U7/U8): U7 corrected from 2716 EPROM to 6810 SRAM. 128 bytes zero page $0000-$007F. CS decode: CS0=NOT A9, CS1=NOT A10, CS2=NOT A11, CS3=VMA/PHI2, CS4=NOT A12, CS5=NOT A7. Mutually exclusive with PIA space via A7. A0-A7 sufficient for identification.

J5.description: Main edge connector - MPU to driver board interface

1.label: D7
notes: Most significant data bit (D7). Physical pin 1 on connector.
ORIENTATION NOTE: J5 numbers data bits in REVERSE -- pin 1 is D7 (MSB), pin 8 is D0 (LSB). Software reading the bus as a flat byte must assemble it as (J5_1 << 7) | (J5_2 << 6) | ... | (J5_8 << 0).

28.label: EXT MEM
notes: EXT MEM -- External memory enable control, internal buffer chain destination.

DO NOT CONNECT to external test equipment. Loading this line (adding any input impedance to the U19B-9 / R15 / R137 node) shifts the buffer chain operating point and causes MPU lockups during memory access cycles.
If a test instrument needs to detect EXT MEM activity, observe the downstream signal at U15D-3 instead -- buffered output, immune to loading on the input pin.

29.label: KEY
notes: KEY -- Mechanical keying position. Pin physically absent on most production boards (gap in the connector for orientation).
DO NOT CONNECT -- no signal present on any board revision.
Unused +5V tap

31.label: GND
notes: GND -- ground reference for J5 signaling.

BOARD REVISION CAVEAT: J5-31 is connected to the board ground plane on most revisions, but on some early production runs this pin carries signals (not ground). Verify continuity from J5-31 to a known-good ground point (e.g. cabinet braid, J4 GND pins) before relying on it.
RECOMMENDED: tie external test equipment to cabinet braid ground or the J4 ground bus, not J5-31.

shared_bus_architecture.description: U11 PB0-PB3 + U11 CB2 are a SHARED physical bus serving TWO destinations simultaneously

destinations.name: Solenoid driver board
destinations.uses: PB0-PB3 as BCD input to 74LS154 decoder, CB2 as a bank/strobe signal
destinations.behavior: The 74LS154 always decodes the current PB0-PB3 BCD to one of 16 outputs. Whichever output is enabled fires its transistor and energizes the corresponding momentary coil. Decoder sees EVERY PB write; software controls whether a coil "fires" by choosing when to drive the BCD and how long to hold it.

destinations.name: Sound board AS-2518-61 (Squawk & Talk)
destinations.uses: PB0-PB3 arrive at sound board J1-1..J1-5 as Sound Select 0..4 (only 0..3 used for EBD); CB2 arrives at sound board J1-8 as Sound Interrupt
destinations.behavior: Sound board 6802 CPU has its own firmware and local PIA. It reads its sound-select input whenever it services the sound-interrupt line. Two consecutive nibbles form an 8-bit command byte (low nibble first, high nibble second per gamefile notes).

shared_bus_architecture.key_point: BOTH destinations receive every U11 PB write and every U11 CB2 pulse. The CPUs disambiguate by software convention, not hardware routing. Monitor cannot determine from a single PB write whether it was INTENDED as solenoid BCD or sound nibble.
decode_implications: Every U11 PB write is simultaneously a solenoid BCD candidate AND one nibble of a potential sound command.
Solenoid decode requires seeing the same BCD repeated (CPU holds the value while coil fires) -- the two-hit filter empirically separates sol fires from single sound nibbles.
Sound decode requires pairing two consecutive PB writes as (low nibble, high nibble) and looking up the combined byte in gamefile sound_commands.
Ambiguous case: two consecutive identical low-value BCD writes (e.g., back-to-back solenoid fires of coil 4) could falsely pair as sound command 0x44. This is rare in practice.

U10_Port_A_multiplexing.summary: Quad-duty PA0-PA4, triple-duty PA5-PA7. All functions share the same PA write cycle; software/hardware context (CRB mode, CA2 state, strobe selection) determines which destination latches the data.

PA0.function_1_switch_strobe: ST0 via CR43 diode + R133 -> J2-1 (column 1)
PA0.function_3_display_latch: Input to U20A (gated with U10 CA2) -> J1-20 latch strobe #1

PA1.function_3_display_latch: Input to U20B -> J1-21 latch strobe #2

PA2.function_3_display_latch: Input to U20C -> J1-22 latch strobe #3

PA3.function_3_display_latch: Input to U20D -> J1-23 latch strobe #4

strobe_coordination: Switch scan: CPU writes PA with one bit low (ST0-ST4), reads PB returns. Only PA0-PA4 reach switch-strobe diodes.
Lamp write (main driver): CPU writes PA with (addr in PA0-PA3, data in PA4-PA7), then toggles U10 CB2 via CRB bit 3 -> MC14514 decoders on main lamp driver latch 4 lamps simultaneously.
Lamp write (aux driver): Same PA pattern, but toggles U11 CA2 via U11 CRA bit 3 -> aux lamp driver latches.

Display write: CPU writes PA with (BCD segment data on PA4-PA7, no address on PA0-PA3 since they gate latch strobes), pulses U10 CA2 high while one of PA0-PA3 or U11 PA0 is asserted -> U20 AND gate fires corresponding latch strobe on J1-20..24.
notes: PA0-PA3 double as switch strobes AND display latch-gate inputs. The CPU manages this by timing: switch strobes drive PB reads, latch-gate writes happen with different CA2 timing.
PA4 uniquely has FOUR roles total (switch + lamp data + display BCD), triple-duty like PA0-PA3 in total unique destinations.
PA5-PA7 are only dual-duty (lamp data + display BCD) -- no switch strobe.

destinations_via_J4_10: Solenoid driver board -- receives as bank/strobe signal
Sound board AS-2518-61 -- receives as J1-8 Sound Interrupt
U11_CB2.runtime_mode: UNKNOWN from schematic alone. CB2 mode is determined at runtime by software writes to U11 CRB bits 5,4,3. Three possibilities per 6821 datasheet: (a) auto-pulse handshake mode CRB[5:4]=10 where CB2 pulses low for one E cycle after each PB access, (b) manual level control mode CRB[5:4]=11 where CB2 level = CRB bit 3, (c) input mode CRB[5]=0. Must observe U11 CRB writes (or snoop reads via firmware) to determine actual mode.
U11_CB2.decode_relevance: The actual CB2 mode determines whether the strobe happens at PB-write time (auto mode) or at CRB-bit-3-toggle time (manual mode). PinballEMT firmware v0.5.7+ snoops CRB reads to keep cache fresh -- fetch /pia_state after boot to see the real runtime value.

scr_refresh_model: Lamps are driven by SCRs (MCR-106, 2N5060 on driver board)

Lamp circuit is powered by half-wave rectified 6.3V AC illumination supply
Each AC zero-crossing turns all SCRs OFF (current = 0)
CPU re-pulses SCR gates each AC half-cycle to maintain "lit" state

Visible implication on bus monitor: "lit" lamps produce repeated identical lamp writes at 60-120Hz refresh rate

power_checks: 2. Battery at U8-22 (VAUX): Should be 3-4V minimum
4. All grounds at TP4: Should be 0V
5. Inspect for shorts before powering up

2. Scope Ï†1 at U9-3: Complementary to Ï†2

2. Scope address bus A0-A14: Changing bit patterns
3. Scope data bus D0-D7: Changing patterns during execution
4. Check R/W at J5-23: Toggles between read (high) and write (low)

memory_checks: 1. Verify ROM chip selects activate during address access
2. Check RAM U8: CE1, CE2 timing correct
3. Data bus: Valid data during ROM reads
5. If memory fails: Check enable chain U19Bâ†’U14Dâ†’U15Câ†’U15D
common_failures: Erratic behavior: Check battery, RAM integrity
Stuck in reset: Check reset circuit, power supply
No memory access: Check VMA, memory enable chain (U19B->U14D->U15C->U15D), chip selects at ROM/RAM
Corrupted scores: Replace battery, verify RAM
Intermittent: Check solder joints, IC sockets, connectors
No switches: Check U10 Port B, switch matrix strobes/returns
No lamps: Check U10/U11 Port A/B outputs, lamp driver board
No displays: Check U11 Port A digit strobes, BCD data
No solenoids: Check U11 Port B outputs, driver board power
recommended_sequence: 2. RESET: Must be high (>4V) for CPU to run
3. Clock: Ï†2 present at U9-37 and J5-27 (~1MHz)
5. Data bus: D0-D7 changing during execution
6. VMA at TP7: Pulsing during memory access
7. If all signals OK but no function: ROM content or CPU failure
8. If specific features fail: Check corresponding PIA and I/O

changelog.rationale: v2.0's deletion of SUPPLEMENT_CRITICAL_ADDITIONS removed 9 R-designators (R6, R8, R9, R13, R21, R22, R23, R54, R134) that were real schematic content. The v1.9 changelog claimed SUPPLEMENT had been reconciled into integrated_circuits, but the consolidation was incomplete and these passive components were still only documented in SUPPLEMENT when v2.0 deleted it. v2.1 restores them by folding them into the appropriate IC entries.
fixes: U9 (CPU): added pin_detail block covering pins 2 (HALT/R135), 3 (PHI1/R9), 4 (IRQ/R134), 5 (VMA/R136), 6 (NMI/R13/S33), 36 (DBE), and 37 (PHI2/R8). Restores all clock buffer resistors and IRQ/NMI passive components.
U10 pin 37 IRQB and pin 38 IRQA: documented as open-drain outputs sharing the R134 4.7K pullup at U9-4 with the U11 IRQ lines.
U11 CA2_pin39: structured to include R54 (470 ohm) series resistor in addition to the existing destination info.

U12 Display Interrupt Generator: added as a proper integrated_circuits.U12 entry with R21 56K, R22 4.7K, R23 1K timing components, output to U11-40, and an explicit chip_identity block marking the part number as UNVERIFIED (documented as '555 timer or similar' since v1.0; definitive identification requires reading the package marking on a real board).
structural_change: tracing_status replaces the flat 'completeness: 5' rating with completeness_by_subsystem, listing each subsystem's confidence, completeness, and outstanding items. This gives a clearer picture of what is and isn't board-repair-grade documentation, and provides hooks for community contributions.
things_I_got_wrong_in_recent_corresponde: Claimed U13 was missing from integrated_circuits. U13 doesn't exist on the AS-2518-35 board -- the IC numbering legitimately skips it. Zero hits across v1.0 through v1.9.
Implied U12 chip identity was a v2.0 omission. It has been documented as '555 timer or similar' across every version since v1.0. It is a longstanding outstanding item, not a recent loss.
Made unused gates on U14/U15/U16 hex inverters sound like a gap. Unused gates are unused; their absence isn't missing content.
changelog.honest_assessment: v2.1 is bus-decode-complete and provides the schematic-derivable facts a board-repair tool needs for the AS-2518-35. The two remaining items (U12 part identification, R6 value) are minor follow-ups rather than gaps in core coverage. Calling this 'diagnostic_complete' is fair for the bus-observer use case; for full component-level repair without external schematic reference, see the per-subsystem completeness ratings above.

changelog.author: Final closure pass on outstanding items
changes: U12 chip identity confirmed: 555 timer in astable configuration. Sole connection is U11-40 (CA1). Status changed from UNVERIFIED to VERIFIED.
R6 value confirmed: 1K. U9 PHI1 pin_detail updated -- previously referenced R6 without a value.

Aux lamp driver board entry removed from completeness_by_subsystem. It is a separate board, not part of the AS-2518-35 MPU profile. The matrix_topology.lamp_matrix forward reference remains as a pointer to the future separate aux driver profile.
Top-level status now DIAGNOSTIC_COMPLETE.
changelog.scope_clarification: DIAGNOSTIC_COMPLETE means: anyone with this profile, the AS-2518-35 schematic, and a multimeter can identify any IC's role, trace any signal path, identify the passive components on critical pins, decode the address space, and execute the diagnostic procedures. It does NOT mean every unused gate of every 7404 hex inverter is individually enumerated -- unused gates are unused, not missing.
